segments: ... with Shawar.
And when they went together and arrived in Egypt,
Shawar knew from the movements of Shirkuh
that he was striving to strip the kingdom from the Egyptians.
And therefore he sent and made peace with the Franks,
and he disregarded Shirkuh,
and did not give him anything that he had promised of gold and renowned places.
Then Shirkuh sent his forces,
and they captured the city of Bilbays.
And Shawar sent and brought the King of Jerusalem with a large force of the Franks.
And Shirkuh went and fortified himself in Bilbays.
And the Egyptians united with the Franks,
and went against him to Bilbays and besieged him there for three months.
And when the news {OCR?} reached them that the Franks had been broken and taken captive at Harem,
the King of Jerusalem sent to Shirkuh
and permitted him to depart in peace and go to his own country,
and to leave Egypt to its owners.
And Shirkuh readily agreed to this,
and went out and departed for Damascus.
And in the year 1476
of the Greeks [1164/1165 AD], Qilij Arslan, Sultan of Iconium, took possession of Geuksun, Ablastha, and Taranta,
and began to persecute the sons of Danishmend.
And Nur al-Din took possession of Banias,
and fortified it well.
And Thoros the Armenian plundered Marash,
and captured four hundred Turks.
And he sent to Nur al-Din:
"If you do not ransom the Christian leaders who are with you,
I will burn all of these in fire."
Then Nur al-Din was compelled,
and he ransomed everyone who was with him, and also the young Prince, for a hundred thousand dinars.
And when this Prince Bohemond was delivered,
he went to the Emperor of the Greeks in Constantinople, who was his brother-in-law;
and much wealth was given to him,
and he came to Antioch,
and brought with him a Greek Patriarch whose name was Athanasius.
And because of this the Patriarch of the Franks became angry,
and went out and took up residence in the fortress of Qusayr,
and sent interdicts against the Frankish Antiochians.
And in this same year, in the month of Shebat, Amin al-Dawlah Ibn al-Talmid, the Christian physician, passed away in Baghdad at the age of ninety years.
This was a man skilled in various sciences:
for in medicine he was the unique one of his time,
and in rhetoric he was likewise well versed,
and in the grammar of the Arabs and their poetry
